1→# Bivvy Development Workflow
     2→
     3→> Atomic development workflow for building Bivvy.
     4→
     5→<steps>
     6→  <step number="1" id="specification">
     7→    <title>Specification</title>
     8→    <goal>Define the contract your code must fulfill before writing implementation.</goal>
     9→    <instructions>
    10→      <instruction>
    11→        Define the Behavior: Create test files first. Tests are the specification.
    12→        <conditional>
    13→          <condition>Test files already exist</condition>
    14→          <action>Update tests to match the new/changed behavior</action>
    15→        </conditional>
    16→      </instruction>
    17→      <instruction>
    18→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    19→        <expected>All new or updated tests should FAIL</expected>
    20→        <rationale>Failing tests prove they're actually testing new logic, not passing by accident.</rationale>
    21→      </instruction>
    22→    </instructions>
    23→    <gate>
    24→      <condition>New tests fail for the right reasons</condition>
    25→      <on_fail>Refine your tests until they correctly specify the behavior</on_fail>
    26→    </gate>
    27→  </step>
    28→
    29→  <step number="2" id="implementation">
    30→    <title>Implementation</title>
    31→    <goal>Write the minimum code to make tests pass.</goal>
    32→    <prerequisite ref="specification">Failing tests from specification step</prerequisite>
    33→    <instructions>
    34→      <instruction>
    35→        Write the Code: Implement only what's needed to pass the tests. Resist adding "nice to have" features.
    36→      </instruction>
    37→      <instruction>
    38→        Keep it Simple: If you're writing more code than tests require, stop and reconsider.
    39→      </instruction>
    40→    </instructions>
    41→    <gate>
    42→      <condition>All tests pass</condition>
    43→      <on_fail>Continue implementing or fix bugs until green</on_fail>
    44→    </gate>
    45→  </step>
    46→
    47→  <step number="3" id="documentation">
    48→    <title>Documentation</title>
    49→    <goal>Document while context is fresh. User-facing and dev-facing docs are separate concerns.</goal>
    50→    <prerequisite ref="implementation">Tests passing</prerequisite>
    51→    <instructions>
    52→      <instruction>
    53→        Rustdoc Comments: Add `///` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules). This is the primary form of API documentation.
    54→      </instruction>
    55→      <instruction>
    56→        User-Facing Docs: Update `docs/` if adding commands, config options, or user-visible features. These are Starlight pages written for end users — never reference internals.
    57→      </instruction>
    58→      <instruction>
    59→        Source READMEs: Update or create `README.md` in source directories (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`) when adding or changing subsystem design, architecture, or guiding principles.
    60→      </instruction>
    61→      <instruction>
    62→        Inline Comments: Add comments only where the "why" isn't obvious from the code.
    63→      </instruction>
    64→      <instruction>
    65→        Verify Docs Build: Confirm documentation compiles without errors.
    66→        <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    67→        <expected>No documentation errors</expected>
    68→      </instruction>
    69→    </instructions>
    70→    <boundaries>
    71→      <rule>Developer docs go in source tree (rustdoc + source READMEs), never in `docs/`</rule>
    72→      <rule>User-facing docs go in `docs/`, never in source READMEs</rule>
    73→    </boundaries>
    74→    <anti-patterns>
    75→      <anti-pattern>Documenting "what" the code does (the code should show that)</anti-pattern>
    76→      <anti-pattern>Leaving documentation for later (it won't happen)</anti-pattern>
    77→      <anti-pattern>Over-commenting obvious code</anti-pattern>
    78→      <anti-pattern>Putting developer architecture docs in `docs/`</anti-pattern>
    79→      <anti-pattern>Putting user-facing guides in source READMEs</anti-pattern>
    80→    </anti-patterns>
    81→  </step>
    82→
    83→  <step number="4" id="linting">
    84→    <title>Static Quality Gate (Linting)</title>
    85→    <goal>Catch issues before they become problems.</goal>
    86→    <prerequisite ref="documentation">Implementation and documentation complete</prerequisite>
    87→    <instructions>
    88→      <instruction>
    89→        <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    90→        <expected>No formatting differences</expected>
    91→        <fix>cargo fmt</fix>
    92→      </instruction>
    93→      <instruction>
    94→        <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    95→        <expected>No warnings or errors</expected>
    96→        <rationale>Warnings today become bugs tomorrow. Zero tolerance. Flags match CI.</rationale>
    97→      </instruction>
    98→    </instructions>
    99→    <gate>
   100→      <condition>Both commands pass with zero output</condition>
   101→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Fix all issues. Return to implementation if code changes are needed.</on_fail>
   102→    </gate>
   103→  </step>
   104→
   105→  <step number="5" id="testing">
   106→    <title>Verification Gate (Full Test Suite)</title>
   107→    <goal>Ensure nothing is broken.</goal>
   108→    <prerequisite ref="linting">Linting passes</prerequisite>
   109→    <critical>
   110→      ALWAYS run `cargo test --all-features` without filters. NEVER use:
   111→      - cargo test some_name
   112→      - cargo test module::
   113→      - cargo test --lib
   114→      The ENTIRE test suite must pass with all features. "X filtered out" means you ran it wrong.
   115→      The --all-features flag matches CI - skipping it locally may cause CI failures.
   116→    </critical>
   117→    <!-- Optimization: cargo llvm-cov already runs the full test suite.
   118→         If tests fail, no TOTAL line is produced and the threshold check fails.
   119→         A separate cargo test is redundant here. -->
   120→    <instructions>
   121→      <instruction>
   122→        <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   123→        <expected>All tests pass, coverage at or above 90%</expected>
   124→        <conditional>
   125→          <condition>cargo-llvm-cov not installed</condition>
   126→          <action>Skip coverage check locally; CI will enforce</action>
   127→        </conditional>
   128→      </instruction>
   129→    </instructions>
   130→    <gate>
   131→      <condition>All tests pass, coverage threshold met</condition>
   132→      <on_fail goto="implementation">Do not proceed with failing tests.</on_fail>
   133→    </gate>
   134→  </step>
   135→
   136→  <step number="6" id="build">
   137→    <title>Integration Gate (Build Verification)</title>
   138→    <goal>Confirm production readiness.</goal>
   139→    <prerequisite ref="testing">All tests passing</prerequisite>
   140→    <instructions>
   141→      <instruction>
   142→        <command>cargo check --all-targets --all-features</command>
   143→        <expected>Check succeeds with no warnings</expected>
   144→        <rationale>Debug targets were already compiled by test and clippy. cargo check validates compilation without redundant codegen/linking.</rationale>
   145→      </instruction>
   146→      <instruction>
   147→        <command>cargo build --release</command>
   148→        <expected>Release build succeeds</expected>
   149→        <rationale>Catches release-only issues (optimizations, LTO problems).</rationale>
   150→      </instruction>
   151→    </instructions>
   152→    <gate>
   153→      <condition>Both builds succeed silently</condition>
   154→      <on_fail goto="linting">Treat warnings as errors. Return to linting or implementation until clean.</on_fail>
   155→    </gate>
   156→  </step>
   157→
   158→  <step number="7" id="commit">
   159→    <title>The Atomic Commit</title>
   160→    <goal>Create a single, complete unit of work.</goal>
   161→    <prerequisite ref="build">All gates passed (lint, test, build)</prerequisite>
   162→    <instructions>
   163→      <instruction>
   164→        Stage Selectively: Add only the files related to this change.
   165→        <command>git add [specific files]</command>
   166→        <anti-pattern>git add -A (may include unrelated changes)</anti-pattern>
   167→      </instruction>
   168→      <instruction>
   169→        Write the Message: Explain WHY, not just WHAT.
   170→        <format>
   171→          <line>Short description in imperative mood, 50 chars or less</line>
   172→          <line></line>
   173→          <line>Longer explanation of why this change was made,</line>
   174→          <line>what problem it solves, and any important context.</line>
   175→          <line>Wrap at 72 characters.</line>
   176→        </format>
   177→        <rules>
   178→          <rule>Imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")</rule>
   179→          <rule>Capitalize first letter, no period at end</rule>
   180→          <rule>No type prefixes (no "feat:", "fix:", etc.)</rule>
   181→        </rules>
   182→      </instruction>
   183→      <instruction>
   184→        Verify Atomicity: This commit should be independently checkable, buildable, testable, and documented.
   185→      </instruction>
   186→    </instructions>
   187→    <gate>
   188→      <condition>Commit contains code + tests + docs for one logical change</condition>
   189→      <on_fail>Split into smaller commits or add missing pieces</on_fail>
   190→    </gate>
   191→  </step>
   192→
   193→  <step number="8" id="post-commit">
   194→    <title>Post-Commit Verification</title>
   195→    <goal>Confirm the commit didn't break anything.</goal>
   196→    <prerequisite ref="commit">Commit created</prerequisite>
   197→    <!-- Optimization: no source code changes between build step and here (only git add/commit).
   198→         A lightweight cargo check confirms compilation still holds post-commit. -->
   199→    <instructions>
   200→      <instruction>
   201→        <command>cargo check --all-features</command>
   202→        <expected>Committed state compiles cleanly</expected>
   203→      </instruction>
   204→      <instruction>
   205→        <command>git log -1 --stat</command>
   206→        <rationale>Review what was actually committed</rationale>
   207→      </instruction>
   208→    </instructions>
   209→  </step>
   210→
   211→  <step number="9" id="transition">
   212→    <title>Transition</title>
   213→    <goal>Clean context switch to next task.</goal>
   214→    <instructions>
   215→      <instruction>
   216→        Clean Slate: Clear your mental context. The previous task is done.
   217→      </instruction>
   218→      <instruction goto="specification">
   219→        Next Task: Pick the next item from your backlog and return to specification.
   220→      </instruction>
   221→    </instructions>
   222→  </step>
   223→</steps>
   224→
   225→<verification-commands>
   226→  <description>Quick reference for all verification commands in order (matches CI):</description>
   227→  <command-sequence>
   228→    <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
   229→    <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
   230→    <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
   231→    <command note="NO FILTERS - run entire suite with all features">cargo test --all-features</command>
   232→    <command>cargo check --all-targets --all-features</command>
   233→    <command>cargo build --release</command>
   234→    <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
   235→  </command-sequence>
   236→  <critical>
   237→    `cargo test --all-features` must be run WITHOUT name filters. Never filter tests.
   238→    Output must show "0 filtered out" - any other number is wrong.
   239→    All flags (--all-targets, --all-features) match CI exactly.
   240→  </critical>
   241→</verification-commands>
   242→
   243→<principles>
   244→  <principle name="Atomic">Each commit is complete and independent</principle>
   245→  <principle name="Test-First">Tests define behavior before implementation</principle>
   246→  <principle name="Zero-Warning">Warnings are errors; fix them immediately</principle>
   247→  <principle name="Document-As-You-Go">Docs are part of the deliverable, not an afterthought</principle>
   248→  <principle name="Small-Steps">Prefer many small commits over few large ones</principle>
   249→</principles>

1→# Bivvy Development Guidelines
     2→
     3→> Cross-language development environment setup automation, built in Rust.
     4→
     5→## Project Overview
     6→
     7→Bivvy is a CLI tool that replaces ad-hoc `bin/setup` scripts with a declarative YAML configuration and a polished interactive CLI experience. It uses a **Template Registry** instead of hardcoded language logic, allowing user overrides at every level.
     8→
     9→<references>
    10→  <reference path="plans/bivvy-plan.md">Full implementation specification</reference>
    11→  <reference path="plans/README.md">Milestone overview and status</reference>
    12→  <reference path=".claude/bivvy-dev-workflow.md">Development workflow (FOLLOW THIS)</reference>
    13→</references>

    15→## Development Workflow
    16→
    17→**Follow the workflow defined in `.claude/bivvy-dev-workflow.md` for all development work.**
    18→
    19→<workflow-summary>
    20→  <step ref="specification">Write failing tests first</step>
    21→  <step ref="implementation">Implement minimum code to pass tests</step>
    22→  <step ref="documentation">Document while context is fresh (rustdoc for APIs, `docs/` for user-facing changes, source READMEs for design)</step>
    23→  <step ref="linting">Pass `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy`</step>
    24→  <step ref="testing">Pass all tests with >90% coverage</step>
    25→  <step ref="build">Verify clean build</step>
    26→  <step ref="commit">Create atomic commit with code + tests + docs</step>
    27→</workflow-summary>
    28→
    29→<verification-commands>
    30→  <command>cargo doc --no-deps --all-features</command>
    31→  <command>cargo fmt -- --check</command>
    32→  <command>cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings</command>
    33→  <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    34→  <command>cargo check --all-targets --all-features</command>
    35→  <command>cargo build --release</command>
    36→  <command>cargo llvm-cov --all-features --fail-under-lines 90</command>
    37→</verification-commands>
    38→
    39→<critical>
    40→  ALWAYS run `cargo test --all-features` without any filters.
    41→
    42→  CORRECT:   cargo test --all-features
    43→  WRONG:     cargo test config
    44→  WRONG:     cargo test schema
    45→  WRONG:     cargo test --lib
    46→  WRONG:     cargo test some_module::
    47→
    48→  Every verification must run the ENTIRE test suite with all features.
    49→  Never filter to "just the relevant tests" - ALL tests must pass before every commit.
    50→
    51→  If you see "X filtered out" in test output, you ran the wrong command.
    52→
    53→  The --all-features and --all-targets flags match what CI runs. If you skip
    54→  them locally, you may push code that fails CI.
    55→</critical>
    56→
    57→<prohibited-behaviors>
    58→  <behavior>Skipping, disabling, or modifying tests to make them pass</behavior>
    59→  <behavior>Creating commits without accompanying tests</behavior>
    60→  <behavior>Moving on to other work when tests are failing</behavior>
    61→  <behavior>Large commits with multiple unrelated changes</behavior>
    62→  <behavior>Straying from the implementation plan without explicit approval</behavior>
    63→  <behavior>Filtering tests when not debugging (e.g., `cargo test config` instead of `cargo test`)</behavior>
    64→</prohibited-behaviors>

    66→## Architecture
    67→
    68→<philosophy>
    69→Bivvy is a **declarative orchestrator**, not a collection of hardcoded scripts:
    70→  <principle>Uses a Template Registry instead of hardcoded language logic</principle>
    71→  <principle>Optionally injects pre-defined YAML templates during `bivvy init`</principle>
    72→  <principle>Allows user overrides at every level</principle>
    73→  <principle>Tracks execution state to enable smart re-runs</principle>
    74→</philosophy>

   125→## Configuration Schema

   151→## Documentation
   152→
   153→Bivvy has two distinct documentation audiences. Keep them separate.

   155→<documentation>
   156→  <audience name="user-facing" path="docs/">
   157→    <description>Pages served by Starlight on Bivvy's website. Written for end users.</description>
   158→    <rule>All user-facing documentation lives in `docs/`</rule>
   159→    <rule>Write for someone who has never seen the source code</rule>
   160→    <rule>Focus on what Bivvy does and how to use it, not how it's built</rule>
   161→    <rule>Follow the structure in `docs/SUMMARY.md`</rule>
   162→    <rule>When adding a new command, feature, or config option, add or update the corresponding `docs/` page</rule>
   163→  </audience>
   164→
   165→  <audience name="dev-facing" path="src/">
   166→    <description>Developer documentation lives inside the source tree. Written for contributors.</description>
   167→    <form name="rustdoc">
   168→      <rule>Add `///` and `//!` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules)</rule>
   169→      <rule>Primary way to document what code does and how to use it</rule>
   170→    </form>
   171→    <form name="source-readmes">
   172→      <description>Higher-level `README.md` files in source directories that document subsystem design. Example: `src/ui/README.md` documents CLX design norms, color assignments, and spinner lifecycle.</description>
   173→      <rule>Place `README.md` files in source directories to document subsystem design (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`, `src/config/README.md`)</rule>
   174→      <rule>Cover: purpose, key modules/files, design decisions, testing guidance, guiding principles</rule>
   175→      <rule>Focus on the "why" and "how it fits together" — leave API details to rustdoc</rule>
   176→    </form>
   177→  </audience>
   178→
   179→  <boundaries>
   180→    <rule>Do NOT put developer documentation in `docs/` — that directory is exclusively for end users</rule>
   181→    <rule>Do NOT put user-facing documentation in source READMEs — point to `docs/` instead</rule>
   182→  </boundaries>
   183→</documentation>

   185→## Coding Standards
   186→
   187→<standards>
   188→  <standard name="error-handling">
   189→    <rule>Use `anyhow::Result` for application errors</rule>
   190→    <rule>Use `thiserror` for library/domain errors</rule>
   191→    <rule>Provide actionable error messages with context</rule>
   192→  </standard>
   193→
   194→  <standard name="output">
   195→    <rule>Support `--verbose`, `--quiet`, `--non-interactive` flags</rule>
   196→    <rule>Mask secrets in all output (`*_KEY`, `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`, etc.)</rule>
   197→    <rule>Use spinners and progress indicators from `indicatif`</rule>
   198→  </standard>
   199→
   200→  <standard name="idempotency">
   201→    <rule>Steps should be safe to re-run</rule>
   202→    <rule>Use `completed_check` to detect if work is already done</rule>
   203→    <rule>Prompt before re-running completed steps (unless `--force`)</rule>
   204→  </standard>
   205→</standards>

   207→## Testing Patterns
   208→
   209→<test-layers>
   210→  <layer name="Unit" tools="cargo test" speed="Fast">
   211→    Individual functions, parsing, logic
   212→  </layer>
   213→  <layer name="Integration" tools="assert_cmd, tempfile" speed="Medium">
   214→    CLI commands, file I/O, config loading
   215→  </layer>
   216→  <layer name="Snapshot" tools="insta" speed="Fast">
   217→    CLI output format, error messages
   218→  </layer>
   219→</test-layers>
   220→
   221→<cli-testing>
   222→  Use `parse_from()` instead of `parse()` in tests and doc examples:
   223→
   224→  ```rust
   225→  // WRONG - reads actual process args, fails in tests
   226→  let cli = Cli::parse();
   227→
   228→  // CORRECT - explicit args, works in tests
   229→  let cli = Cli::parse_from(["bivvy", "run", "--verbose"]);
   230→  ```
   231→
   232→  This applies to:
   233→  - Unit tests for CLI parsing
   234→  - Doc tests / examples in rustdoc
   235→  - Any test that needs to verify CLI behavior
   236→
   237→  Only use `Cli::parse()` in the actual `main()` function.
   238→</cli-testing>
   239→
   240→<doc-test-guidelines>
   241→  Doc tests should be self-contained and runnable whenever possible.
   242→
   243→  PREFER runnable examples with real test fixtures:
   244→  ```rust
   245→  /// ```
   246→  /// use bivvy::config::load_merged_config;
   247→  /// use tempfile::TempDir;
   248→  /// use std::fs;
   249→  ///
   250→  /// // Create real test files
   251→  /// let temp = TempDir::new().unwrap();
   252→  /// fs::create_dir_all(temp.path().join(".bivvy")).unwrap();
   253→  /// fs::write(temp.path().join(".bivvy/config.yml"), "app_name: test").unwrap();
   254→  ///

- **`~/.bivvy/config.yml`** - User's global configuration
- **`~/.bivvy/templates/`** - User-local templates
- **`~/.bivvy/projects/`** - Project state directory
- **`~/.bivvy/projects/{hash}/state.yml`** - Per-project state storage
- **`~/.bivvy/projects/index.yml`** - Global project index

- **Session store:** `dirs::data_local_dir()/bivvy/sessions/` - Session history
- **Feedback store:** `dirs::data_local_dir()/bivvy/feedback.jsonl` - User feedback
- **Cache dir:** `dirs::cache_dir()/bivvy/templates/` - Remote template cache
- **Update check:** `dirs::cache_dir()/bivvy/update_check.json` - Version update tracking

1. **`src/config/loader.rs`** (Lines 1-120)
   - Implements `ConfigPaths::discover()` and `find_project_root()`
   - Hard-coded merge order: Remote → User Global (`~/.bivvy/config.yml`) → Project → Local
   - Uses `dirs::home_dir()` for user global config

2. **`src/state/store.rs`** (Lines 118-124, 127-129)
   - `StateStore::state_dir()` → `~/.bivvy/projects/{hash}/`
   - Uses `dirs::home_dir()` directly without fallback handling

   - `ProjectIndex::file_path()` → `~/.bivvy/projects/index.yml`
   - Uses `dirs::home_dir().unwrap_or_else()` with fallback to `"~"`

4. **`src/cache/mod.rs`** (Lines 17-22)
   - `default_cache_dir()` → `dirs::cache_dir()/bivvy/templates/`
   - Uses `dirs::cache_dir()` for platform-aware caching

5. **`src/session/mod.rs`** (Lines 17-23)
   - `default_store_path()` → `dirs::data_local_dir()/bivvy/sessions/`

   - Uses `dirs::home_dir()` to find shell config files

**What's Done Well:**
- Uses `dirs` crate (respects XDG on Linux, standard locations on macOS/Windows)
- Proper platform abstraction for cache/data directories
- Atomic file writes with temp-then-rename pattern
- Fallback strategies when `dirs::home_dir()` returns `None`

1→# State Management
     2→
     3→Bivvy tracks execution state to enable smart re-runs, skip completed steps, and detect when watched files have changed.
     4→
     5→## How State Works
     6→
     7→When you run Bivvy, it:
     8→
     9→1. Identifies your project using a hash of the path and git remote
    10→2. Loads any existing state from `~/.bivvy/projects/{hash}/`
    11→3. Tracks which steps run, skip, or fail
    12→4. Saves state after each workflow execution
    13→
    14→## Project Identification
    15→
    16→Projects are uniquely identified by combining:
    17→
    18→- The absolute path to the project root
    19→- The git remote URL (if available)
    20→
    21→This produces a stable hash used as the state directory name, ensuring state persists even if you rename the project folder (as long as the git remote stays the same).
    22→
    23→## Step State
    24→
    25→Bivvy tracks the following for each step:
    26→
    27→| Field | Description |
    28→|-------|-------------|
    29→| `last_run` | When the step last executed |
    30→| `status` | Success, Failed, Skipped, or NeverRun |
    31→| `duration_ms` | How long execution took |
    32→| `watches_hash` | Hash of watched files at last run |
    33→
    34→### Step Status Values
    35→
    36→- **Success** - Step completed without errors
    37→- **Failed** - Step exited with non-zero code or error
    38→- **Skipped** - Step was skipped (already complete or user choice)
    39→- **NeverRun** - Step has never been executed
    40→
    41→## Run History
    42→
    43→Each workflow execution is recorded with:
    44→
    45→```yaml
    46→timestamp: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z
    47→workflow: default
    48→duration_ms: 45000
    49→status: Success
    50→steps_run:
    51→  - dependencies
    52→  - database
    53→steps_skipped:
    54→  - seeds
    55→error: null
    56→```
    57→
    58→### Run Status Values
    59→
    60→- **Success** - All steps completed successfully
    61→- **Failed** - One or more steps failed
    62→- **Interrupted** - Execution was cancelled (Ctrl+C)
    63→
    64→## Change Detection
    65→
    66→When a step has `watches` configured, Bivvy detects if those files have changed since the step last ran:
    67→
    68→```yaml
    69→steps:
    70→  dependencies:
    71→    command: bundle install
    72→    watches:
    73→      - Gemfile
    74→      - Gemfile.lock
    75→```
    76→
    77→Change detection checks:
    78→
    79→1. File modification time vs. step last run time
    80→2. Content hash for files under 1MB
    81→
    82→If watched files have changed, the step is marked as "stale" and will re-run even if previously successful.
    83→
    84→## Preferences
    85→
    86→User choices are saved in `preferences.yml`:
    87→
    88→```yaml
    89→prompts:
    90→  db_name: myapp_development
    91→  install_mode: frozen
    92→
    93→skip_behavior:
    94→  seeds: skip_only
    95→
    96→template_sources:
    97→  rails: builtin
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Saved Preferences
   101→
   102→| Type | Purpose |
   103→|------|---------|
   104→| `prompts` | Answers to interactive prompts |
   105→| `skip_behavior` | How to handle skipped steps |
   106→| `template_sources` | Which template source to use on collision |
   107→
   108→## State File Locations
   109→
   110→| File | Location |
   111→|------|----------|
   112→| State | `~/.bivvy/projects/{hash}/state.yml` |
   113→| Preferences | `~/.bivvy/projects/{hash}/preferences.yml` |
   114→| Project Index | `~/.bivvy/projects/index.yml` |
   115→
   116→## History Pruning
   117→
   118→Bivvy automatically manages state file size:
   119→
   120→- Default retention: 50 runs
   121→- Orphaned step state (not in recent runs) is cleaned up
   122→- Use `bivvy history --prune` to manually clean old history
   123→
   124→## Querying State
   125→
   126→### Last Run
   127→
   128→```bash
   129→bivvy last
   130→```
   131→
   132→Shows details of the most recent run including duration, status, and which steps executed.
   133→
   134→### Full History
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→bivvy history
   138→```
   139→
   140→Shows a table of recent runs with timestamps and outcomes.
   141→
   142→### Step History
   143→
   144→```bash
   145→bivvy history --step dependencies
   146→```
   147→
   148→Shows execution history for a specific step across all runs.
   149→
   150→## Clearing State
   151→
   152→To reset state and force all steps to re-run:
   153→
   154→```bash
   155→bivvy run --force
   156→```
   157→
   158→Or clear state for a specific step:
   159→
   160→```bash
   161→bivvy run --force --step dependencies
   162→```
   163→

1→# Configuration
     2→
     3→Bivvy uses YAML configuration files to define your project setup.
     4→
     5→## File Locations
     6→
     7→Configuration is loaded and merged in this order (later overrides earlier):
     8→
     9→1. Remote base configs (from `extends:`)
    10→2. User global config (`~/.bivvy/config.yml`)
    11→3. Project config (`.bivvy/config.yml`)
    12→4. Local overrides (`.bivvy/config.local.yml`) - gitignored
    13→
    14→## Basic Structure
    15→
    16→```yaml
    17→app_name: "MyApp"
    18→
    19→settings:
    20→  default_output: verbose  # verbose | quiet | silent
    21→
    22→steps:
    23→  install_deps:
    24→    command: "npm install"
    25→
    26→workflows:
    27→  default:
    28→    steps: [install_deps]
    29→```
    30→
    31→## Variable Interpolation
    32→
    33→Use `${VAR}` syntax to interpolate values:
    34→
    35→```yaml
    36→steps:
    37→  setup:
    38→    command: "echo Setting up ${project_name}"
    39→```
    40→
    41→### Built-in Variables
    42→
    43→| Variable | Description |
    44→|----------|-------------|
    45→| `${project_name}` | Directory name of the project |
    46→| `${project_root}` | Absolute path to project root |
    47→
    48→### Environment Variables
    49→
    50→Environment variables are available for interpolation:
    51→
    52→```yaml
    53→steps:
    54→  deploy:
    55→    command: "deploy --env ${RAILS_ENV}"
    56→```
    57→
    58→### Escaping
    59→
    60→Use `$${` to escape (outputs literal `${`):
    61→
    62→```yaml
    63→steps:
    64→  example:
    65→    command: "echo '$${NOT_INTERPOLATED}'"  # outputs: ${NOT_INTERPOLATED}
    66→```
    67→
    68→## Deep Merge Behavior
    69→
    70→When multiple config files define the same key:
    71→
    72→- **Objects**: Recursively merged (nested keys combined)
    73→- **Arrays**: Replaced entirely (not concatenated)
    74→- **Scalars**: Later value wins
    75→
    76→```yaml
    77→# .bivvy/config.yml
    78→steps:
    79→  deps:
    80→    command: "yarn install"
    81→    env:
    82→      NODE_ENV: development
    83→
    84→# .bivvy/config.local.yml
    85→steps:
    86→  deps:
    87→    env:
    88→      NODE_ENV: production
    89→      # command is preserved from base
    90→```
    91→
    92→## Next Steps
    93→
    94→- [Steps Configuration](steps.md)
    95→- [Workflows Configuration](workflows.md)
    96→- [Completed Checks](completed-checks.md)

1→# Templates
     2→
     3→Templates define reusable setup steps. Bivvy includes 20 built-in templates covering system package managers, version managers, and language-specific dependency tools. You can also create custom templates.
     4→
     5→## Using Templates
     6→
     7→Reference a template in your step configuration:
     8→
     9→```yaml
    10→steps:
    11→  deps:
    12→    template: yarn
    13→```
    14→
    15→When you run `bivvy init`, templates are auto-detected based on files in your project (e.g., `Gemfile` triggers the `bundler` template, `package-lock.json` triggers `npm`).
    16→
    17→## Available Built-in Templates
    18→
    19→| Category | Templates |
    20→|----------|-----------|
    21→| System | `brew`, `apt`, `yum`, `pacman` |
    22→| Windows | `chocolatey`, `scoop` |
    23→| Version managers | `mise`, `asdf`, `volta` |
    24→| Ruby | `bundler` |
    25→| Node.js | `yarn`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `bun` |
    26→| Python | `pip`, `poetry`, `uv` |
    27→| Rust | `cargo` |
    28→| Go | `go` |
    29→| Swift | `swift` |
    30→
    31→See [Built-in Templates](builtin.md) for full details on each template.
    32→
    33→## Template Resolution Order
    34→
    35→Templates are resolved in this order (first match wins):
    36→
    37→1. **Project templates** - `.bivvy/templates/steps/`
    38→2. **User templates** - `~/.bivvy/templates/steps/`
    39→3. **Remote templates** - Fetched from configured sources
    40→4. **Built-in templates** - Bundled with Bivvy
    41→
    42→## Overriding Template Values
    43→
    44→Override any template field in your step config:
    45→
    46→```yaml
    47→steps:
    48→  deps:
    49→    template: yarn
    50→    command: "yarn install --frozen-lockfile"  # override default command
    51→```
    52→
    53→## Template Inputs
    54→
    55→Some templates accept inputs for customization:
    56→
    57→```yaml
    58→steps:
    59→  db:
    60→    template: postgres
    61→    inputs:
    62→      database_name: myapp_dev
    63→      port: 5433
    64→```
    65→
    66→## Creating Custom Templates
    67→
    68→Create `.bivvy/templates/steps/<name>.yml`:
    69→
    70→```yaml
    71→name: my-template
    72→description: "My custom setup step"
    73→category: custom
    74→
    75→inputs:
    76→  env:
    77→    description: "Environment name"
    78→    type: string
    79→    default: development
    80→
    81→step:
    82→  title: "Run my setup"
    83→  command: "my-setup --env ${env}"
    84→  completed_check:
    85→    type: file_exists
    86→    path: ".setup-complete"
    87→```
    88→
    89→## Next Steps
    90→
    91→- [Built-in Templates](builtin.md)
    92→- [Custom Templates](custom.md)

1→# Bivvy Development Workflow
     2→
     3→> Atomic development workflow for building Bivvy.
     4→
     5→<steps>
     6→  <step number="1" id="specification">
     7→    <title>Specification</title>
     8→    <goal>Define the contract your code must fulfill before writing implementation.</goal>
     9→    <instructions>
    10→      <instruction>
    11→        Define the Behavior: Create test files first. Tests are the specification.
    12→        <conditional>
    13→          <condition>Test files already exist</condition>
    14→          <action>Update tests to match the new/changed behavior</action>
    15→        </conditional>
    16→      </instruction>
    17→      <instruction>
    18→        <command>cargo test --all-features</command>
    19→        <expected>All new or updated tests should FAIL</expected>
    20→        <rationale>Failing tests prove they're actually testing new logic, not passing by accident.</rationale>
    21→      </instruction>
    22→    </instructions>
    23→    <gate>
    24→      <condition>New tests fail for the right reasons</condition>
    25→      <on_fail>Refine your tests until they correctly specify the behavior</on_fail>
    26→    </gate>
    27→  </step>
    28→
    29→  <step number="2" id="implementation">
    30→    <title>Implementation</title>
    31→    <goal>Write the minimum code to make tests pass.</goal>
    32→    <prerequisite ref="specification">Failing tests from specification step</prerequisite>
    33→    <instructions>
    34→      <instruction>
    35→        Write the Code: Implement only what's needed to pass the tests. Resist adding "nice to have" features.
    36→      </instruction>
    37→      <instruction>
    38→        Keep it Simple: If you're writing more code than tests require, stop and reconsider.
    39→      </instruction>
    40→    </instructions>
    41→    <gate>
    42→      <condition>All tests pass</condition>
    43→      <on_fail>Continue implementing or fix bugs until green</on_fail>
    44→    </gate>
    45→  </step>
    46→
    47→  <step number="3" id="documentation">
    48→    <title>Documentation</title>
    49→    <goal>Document while context is fresh. User-facing and dev-facing docs are separate concerns.</goal>
    50→    <prerequisite ref="implementation">Tests passing</prerequisite>
    51→    <instructions>
    52→      <instruction>
    53→        Rustdoc Comments: Add `///` doc comments to all public items (structs, functions, modules). This is the primary form of API documentation.
    54→      </instruction>
    55→      <instruction>
    56→        User-Facing Docs: Update `docs/` if adding commands, config options, or user-visible features. These are Starlight pages written for end users — never reference internals.
    57→      </instruction>
    58→      <instruction>
    59→        Source READMEs: Update or create `README.md` in source directories (e.g., `src/cli/README.md`) when adding or changing subsystem design, architecture, or guiding principles.
    60→      </instruction>
    61→      <instruction>
    62→        Inline Comments: Add comments only where the "why" isn't obvious from the code.
    63→      </instruction>

# Replace hardcoded ~/.bivvy paths with platform-standard directories

## Context

Multiple modules resolve system paths by calling `dirs::home_dir().join(".bivvy")` directly, producing `~/.bivvy/` on all platforms. This ignores XDG conventions on Linux and platform-native directories on macOS/Windows. Some modules (cache, session, feedback) already use `dirs::cache_dir()` and `dirs::data_local_dir()` correctly, but there's no centralized module — so each call site duplicates logic and none supports a `BIVVY_HOME` override.

**Goal:** Create a single `src/dirs.rs` module that is the source of truth for all Bivvy system paths, using proper platform directories, with a `BIVVY_HOME` env var override for backward compatibility.

## XDG/Platform Mapping

| Purpose | `BIVVY_HOME` set | Linux | macOS | Windows |
|---------|-----------------|-------|-------|---------|
| Config | `$BIVVY_HOME/` | `~/.config/bivvy/` | `~/Library/Application Support/bivvy/` | `%APPDATA%\bivvy\` |
| Data | `$BIVVY_HOME/` | `~/.local/share/bivvy/` | `~/Library/Application Support/bivvy/` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bivvy\` |
| Cache | `$BIVVY_HOME/` | `~/.cache/bivvy/` | `~/Library/Caches/bivvy/` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bivvy\` |

When `BIVVY_HOME` is set, all three collapse to that single directory — matching the old `~/.bivvy/` layout exactly.

---

## Commit 1: Create `src/dirs.rs` with `BivvyDirs` struct and tests

### New file: `src/dirs.rs`

A `BivvyDirs` struct with three `PathBuf` fields (`config_dir`, `data_dir`, `cache_dir`) and these methods:

| Method | Base | Path |
|--------|------|------|
| `user_config_file()` | config | `config.yml` |
| `user_templates_dir()` | config | `templates/` |
| `project_state_dir(hash)` | data | `projects/{hash}/` |
| `project_index_file()` | data | `projects/index.yml` |
| `failure_reports_dir()` | data | `failure-reports/` |
| `sessions_dir()` | data | `sessions/` |
| `feedback_file()` | data | `feedback.jsonl` |
| `resume_state_file()` | data | `resume-state.json` |
| `template_cache_dir()` | cache | `templates/` |
| `remote_config_cache_dir()` | cache | `remote-configs/` |
| `update_check_file()` | cache | `update_check.json` |

- `from_env()` — checks `BIVVY_HOME`, falls back to `dirs::config_dir()` / `dirs::data_local_dir()` / `dirs::cache_dir()`
- `Default` impl calls `from_env()`

- All accessor methods return expected path suffixes using `BivvyDirs::new()` with a tempdir
- `BIVVY_HOME` override collapses all dirs to one root (test via `new()`, not env var)
- `from_env()` without `BIVVY_HOME` returns paths containing "bivvy"
